info.name: Aastrika AI Studio — via uiproxy
info.description:
AI Studio **through the uiproxy**, not the AI service directly.

Every route here is `/protected/v8/aiStudio/*` on the portal, which forwards to the AI service
via Kong. If you want the service's own API, use the `Aastrika AI Service` collection instead —
the two are not interchangeable, because the authentication and the identity handling differ.

## Before you start

Two variables, both under Collection → Variables → **CURRENT VALUE**:

| Variable | What to put in it |
|---|---|
| `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:3003/apis` locally, or your portal host + `/apis` |
| `sessionId` | The `connect.sid` cookie value from a logged-in portal tab |

`rootOrg` defaults to `aastar`; change it if you are on another tenant.

To get `sessionId`: sign in to the portal, open DevTools → Application → Cookies, copy the
whole `connect.sid` value including the `s%3A` prefix.

## If the portal will not start locally

`npm run start:dev` needs Cassandra on 9042 (the session store) and a reachable Keycloak, and
it binds port 3003 — which may already be taken. If that is in the way, the repo has a runner
that serves these same paths with neither dependency:

```
npm run dev:aiStudio          # or PORT=4010 npm run dev:aiStudio
```

Point `baseUrl` at `http://localhost:3005/apis` and **clear the `sessionId` variable** — that
runner supplies the session itself, so no cookie is needed. Everything past that point is the
real path: the same router, the same headers, the same Kong route.

Use the full portal when you need to prove the Keycloak hop; use the runner for everything else.

## Authentication — the session cookie, nothing else

The portal authenticates with Keycloak, so these routes need **your portal session** and
nothing more. Collection-level auth sends it on every request; individual requests inherit it.

**Do not send a creator, a username, or any identity header.** The proxy reads the signed-in
user from your Keycloak session and sends `x-aastrika-creator` to the AI service itself,
overwriting anything you supply. That is deliberate: it is what stops one user recording spend
against another. It also adds the gateway key (`Authorization`) — a server-side credential that
never reaches a browser.

So the client side is one cookie, and the proxy handles the rest.

## What the proxy does and does not do

- **Does not validate bodies.** Which fields an endpoint requires is the AI service's rule, so a
  request is forwarded as it arrives and the service's own error is relayed with its status and
  message intact. A 422 for thin material, a 400 `SOURCE_MISSING`, a 403 on someone else's
  content all reach you unchanged.
- **Does not rewrite bodies.** What you send is what the AI service receives, byte for byte.
- **Forwards anything it does not recognise.** An endpoint the AI service adds later is
  reachable here the day it ships, under the same path shape.

## Cost

One request spends money: **2.5 Generate video**. Everything else, planning and revising
included, is free. Check `costEstimate.totalUsd` from 2.3 before running it.

## Order

Requests are numbered in the order they chain, and each saves what the next needs into
collection variables — so a folder runs top to bottom without copying ids by hand. 2.1 sets
`studioSourceId`; 2.3 sets `jobId`; 3.2 sets `sourceId`; 3.3 sets `quizJobId`; 4.1 sets
`contentId` and `artifactFilename`.

Requests that upload a file are marked **(pick a file)**: Postman cannot ship one for you, so
open the Body tab and choose one.

**Start with 3.1 List languages** — no arguments, spends nothing, and tells you whether the
whole chain is wired up.
---

*Every request in this collection was run end to end against the deployed Kong route
(`https://sphere.aastrika.org/api/ai-studio`) on 2026-09-18: 21 of 22 routes verified working.
The exception is `2.5 Generate video`, which was deliberately not run because it is the one
call that spends real money.*

item.name: 2 · AI Studio — document to video
item.description: Plan first, produce second. `Generate plan` writes only a script and a cost estimate. `Generate video` is the step that actually spends.

request.description:
Source material for a video.

`kind` selects the handling:

- `document` — PDF/DOCX/TXT parsed to text, PDF pages rendered as slides
- `image` — a diagram or photo for one scene
- `reference-video` — a video whose look and pacing to copy

Upload a **video** with `kind=document` and it comes back split into segments with a transcript: that is edit mode.

Saves `studioSourceId` for 2.3.

**No creator field, no identity header.** The proxy reads the signed-in user from your Keycloak session and sends `x-aastrika-creator` itself, overwriting anything you send. Sending it here does nothing.

formdata.description: PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD, SRT — or a video (MP4/MOV/WEBM) to edit instead

request.description: The roster depends on which provider keys the AI service has. Use an `id` from here as `voicePref` when planning.

Writes the script and a cost estimate. **Free** — nothing is generated and nothing is billed. Show `costEstimate.totalUsd` before running 2.5.

Only `docText` and `userPrompt` are required; delete any line you do not need. The proxy does not validate the body — it forwards what you send and relays the AI service's own error, so a missing field comes back with the service's message.

**sourceId** — from 2.1. Without it a scene planned against a slide page cannot find that page at render time.
**videoType** — `watercolor` | `slides` | `roleplay` | `translation` | `videoedit`
**language** — `hi` | `en` | `kn` | `te`
**depth** — `brief` | `standard` | `detailed`
**voicePref** — a voice id from 2.2
**useSourceSlides** — use the PDF's own pages instead of generated art; needs `sourceId`

Edit mode: set `videoType` to `videoedit`, drop `docText`, and send `videoMeta`.

**No creator field, no identity header.** The proxy reads the signed-in user from your Keycloak session and sends `x-aastrika-creator` itself, overwriting anything you send. Sending it here does nothing.

body.raw:
{
  "docText": "Postpartum haemorrhage is a leading cause of maternal mortality in India. Active management of the third stage of labour reduces this risk. Administer oxytocin within one minute of birth. Watch for danger signs: heavy bleeding, fever, severe headache. Refer immediately if any appear.",
  "userPrompt": "A short training video for ANMs and nurses",
  "sourceId": "{{studioSourceId}}",
  "videoType": "watercolor",
  "language": "hi",
  "filename": "postpartum-care.pdf",
  "contentName": "प्रसव के बाद की देखभाल",
  "depth": "standard",
  "aspectRatio": "16:9",
  "voicePref": "NS2XUDKoFptzsjBWNOWe",
  "pages": 3,
  "useSourceSlides": false,
  "styleGuide": "Warm watercolour, Indian rural clinic setting, no text in the images",
  "userImages": []
}

item.name: 3 · Quiz — sources to MCQs
item.description: Sources in, validated MCQs out. **3.1 is the smoke test** — run it first.

request.description:
**Start here.** No arguments, spends nothing — the cheapest way to confirm the whole chain (portal → Kong → AI service) is wired up.

`401`/`419` means the cookie is stale. `404` means Kong has no `/ai-studio` route or is not stripping the prefix. `500` means the proxy reached Kong but the hop failed — check the uiproxy logs for `AI Studio quiz/languages`.

exec: pm.test('the whole chain is up', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description:
Files and/or links in, parsed text out. Video and audio are transcribed automatically.

A source that failed to read comes back with an `error` instead of `chars` — show it and leave it unticked rather than dropping it silently.

Saves the first readable `sourceId`.

formdata.description: PDF, DOCX, TXT — or video/audio, which is transcribed
Optional, one per line. Drive links must be shared as 'Anyone with the link'.

request.description:
Run 3.2 first so `sourceId` is set.

At least one of `sourceIds`, `docText` or `sourceJobId` is required — the empty ones below are placeholders, so delete what you do not use. They combine: all three are concatenated into the material.

**sourceJobId** — a finished video's job id, to build questions from that video's script.
**language** — `hi` | `en` | `kn` | `te`
**numQuestions** — 1-60 (default 10)
**numOptions** — 2-6 (default 4)
**difficulty** — `mixed` | `easy` | `medium` | `hard`
**bloom** — `mixed` | `remember` | `understand` | `apply`

A **422** is deliberate, not a failure: the material was too thin for the number of questions asked for, and the message says how many it can support. The proxy relays it intact — show it verbatim rather than retrying blindly.

An unknown source id is a **400 SOURCE_MISSING**.

**No creator field, no identity header.** The proxy reads the signed-in user from your Keycloak session and sends `x-aastrika-creator` itself, overwriting anything you send. Sending it here does nothing.

item.name: 5 · Usage & spend — the dashboard
item.description: Two endpoints, five ways of calling them. The POST is the one to build a dashboard on.

item.name: 5.1 Full report  (POST — the one to build on)

request.description:
All supported filters, shown empty. An empty string is treated as absent, so this body as-is returns everything.

**creator** — one creator (`user` is accepted as its former name)
**type** — `video` | `assessment` (`quiz` also accepted)
**status** — `created` | `planned` | `rendering` | `done` | `failed`
**from**, **to** — ISO dates, inclusive
**limit** — default 100, max 1000; `0` returns totals with no rows
**offset** — for paging

A malformed filter is a **400 INVALID_QUERY** naming the field — never silently ignored, because a spend report that quietly answers a different question than the one asked is worse than one that fails.

In the response, `page.total` counts everything matching the filter, not just this page; `costEstimated: true` on an item means the figure was back-estimated.

item.name: 5.2 Filtered — videos finished in a month

request.description:
Filters combine, so this is every finished video in the date range.

**`creator` ships blank**, and an empty string is treated as absent — so as-is this covers all creators. Put a username in the `creator` collection variable to scope it to one person; the name to use is whatever the Creator column in 5.1 shows, since that is what the proxy recorded from the session.

The dates are fixed rather than relative. Change them to a range you actually have data in.

**creator** — one creator (`user` is accepted as its former name)
**type** — `video` | `assessment` (`quiz` also accepted)
**status** — `created` | `planned` | `rendering` | `done` | `failed`
**from**, **to** — ISO dates, inclusive
**limit** — default 100, max 1000; `0` returns totals with no rows
**offset** — for paging

A malformed filter is a **400 INVALID_QUERY** naming the field — never silently ignored, because a spend report that quietly answers a different question than the one asked is worse than one that fails.
